description_full: Strathcona Resources Ltd. acquires, explores, develops, and produces petroleum and natural gas reserves in Canada. It operates through three segments: Cold Lake, Lloydminster Thermal and Lloydminster Conventional segments. The Cold Lake Thermal segment includes three producing assets in the Cold Lake region of Alberta; Lindbergh, Orion, and Tucker. The Lloydminster Thermal segment comprises thermal oil assets in the Lloydminster region, consisting of multiple SAGD projects in southwestern Saskatchewan. The Lloydminster Conventional segment comprises conventional oil operations, primarily located in southwestern Saskatchewan and extending into adjacent areas of southeast Alberta. The company was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Calgary, Canada.

financial_summary: STRATHCONA RES LTD. is a mid-cap energy business with a $5.5B market cap on $3.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -4% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 25% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $93M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.58× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 7.2×.

Management returns a meaningful 30.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.3% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
